title: Composition preserves relative tensor-action identities
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Let $P:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ and $Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be strong monoidal functors [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], with inverse tensor comparisons $\mu^P,\mu^Q$. Let $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be functors. Suppose given maps, natural in both arguments,
$$\pi_{A,N}:RA\otimes N\longrightarrow R(A\otimes PN),\qquad
\delta_{M,B}:JM\otimes B\longrightarrow J(M\otimes QB),$$
for all $A,B\in\mathcal D$, $M\in\mathcal C$ and $N\in\mathcal E$.
For a functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, a strong monoidal functor $S:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ with inverse tensor comparison $\mu^S$, and maps $a_{M,N}:FM\otimes N\to F(M\otimes SN)$, the tensor-action identity means
$$F\bigl((\alpha^{\mathcal A}_{M,SN,ST})^{-1}\circ(1_M\otimes\mu^S_{N,T})\bigr)\circ a_{M,N\otimes T}\circ\alpha^{\mathcal B}_{FM,N,T}
=a_{M\otimes SN,T}\circ(a_{M,N}\otimes1_T)$$
for all $M,N,T$. Assume this identity holds for $(R,P,\pi)$ and $(J,Q,\delta)$.
Put $H=RJ$, $S=QP$, give $S$ the inverse comparison
$$\mu^S_{N,T}=\mu^Q_{PN,PT}\circ Q(\mu^P_{N,T}),$$
and define $\tau_{M,N}=R(\delta_{M,PN})\circ\pi_{JM,N}:HM\otimes N\to H(M\otimes SN)$. Then $\tau$ is natural and satisfies the tensor-action identity for $(H,S,\tau)$.
More explicitly, writing $M_1=M\otimes QPN_1$, the following equality holds after the canonical associators (the displayed targets use left association):
$$\tau_{M_1,N_2}\circ(\tau_{M,N_1}\otimes1)
=R\bigl(\delta_{M_1,PN_2}\circ(\delta_{M,PN_1}\otimes1)\bigr)\circ\pi_{JM\otimes PN_1,N_2}\circ(\pi_{JM,N_1}\otimes1).$$
None of $\pi,\delta,\tau$ need be invertible. No adjunctions, symmetry, or unit equation for these transformations are assumed.

source.place: Tags 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, and 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent-written abstract composition calculation for the proper/open composite, extracted from returned proof Step 8

proof.text:
Write composition right to left as in [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. For $a:M\to M'$ and $b:N\to N'$, the two given naturality equations and functoriality give
$$\begin{aligned}
H(a\otimes QP(b))\tau_{M,N}
&=R(\delta_{M',PN'})R(J(a)\otimes P(b))\pi_{JM,N}\\
&=R(\delta_{M',PN'})\pi_{JM',N'}(H(a)\otimes b)
=\tau_{M',N'}(H(a)\otimes b).
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality uses naturality of $\delta$ at $(a,P(b))$ inside $R$; the second uses naturality of $\pi$ at $(J(a),b)$. This proves naturality of $\tau$ without an invertibility assumption.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category) and 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent-written calculation from the displayed hypotheses; calculation Step 1

proof.text:
Fix $M,N,T$ and put $A=JM$, $X=PN$, $Y=PT$, $V=P(N\otimes T)$, $u=\mu^P_{N,T}:V\to X\otimes Y$, $q=\mu^Q_{X,Y}$ and $M_1=M\otimes QX$. These inverse comparisons have the directions specified in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Introduce the actual morphisms
$$b_A=(\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{A,X,Y})^{-1}(1_A\otimes u):A\otimes V\to(A\otimes X)\otimes Y,$$
$$c=(\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{M,QX,QY})^{-1}(1_M\otimes q):M\otimes Q(X\otimes Y)\to M_1\otimes QY,$$
$$b_M=c(1_M\otimes Q(u)):M\otimes QV\to M_1\otimes QY.$$
Bifunctoriality of tensor shows that $b_M=(\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{M,SN,ST})^{-1}(1_M\otimes\mu^S_{N,T})$, since the prescribed $\mu^S$ is $qQ(u)$. No implicit identification of parenthesizations is used here.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category) and 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent-written calculation from the displayed hypotheses; calculation Step 2

proof.text:
Set $W=\tau_{M_1,T}(\tau_{M,N}\otimes1_T)$. Expand both occurrences of $\tau$. Naturality of $\pi$ in its first argument, applied to the arrow $\delta_{M,X}:A\otimes X\to JM_1$, gives
$$\pi_{JM_1,T}(R(\delta_{M,X})\otimes1_T)=R(\delta_{M,X}\otimes1_Y)\pi_{A\otimes X,T}.$$
Using the tensor bifunctor law of [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and the composition law of $R$, obtain
$$W=R\bigl(\delta_{M_1,Y}(\delta_{M,X}\otimes1_Y)\bigr)\pi_{A\otimes X,T}(\pi_{A,N}\otimes1_T).$$
This is precisely the additional explicit equality in the statement, with $N_1=N$, $N_2=T$; both sides land in $H(M_1\otimes QY)$.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category) and 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent-written calculation from the displayed hypotheses; calculation Step 3

proof.text:
The assumed action identity for $(R,P,\pi)$, evaluated at $(A,N,T)$, reads exactly
$$\pi_{A\otimes X,T}(\pi_{A,N}\otimes1_T)=R(b_A)\pi_{A,N\otimes T}\alpha^{\mathcal E}_{RA,N,T}.$$
Substituting this equality into Step 3 and using functoriality gives
$$W=R\bigl(\delta_{M_1,Y}(\delta_{M,X}\otimes1_Y)b_A\bigr)\pi_{A,N\otimes T}\alpha^{\mathcal E}_{HM,N,T}.$$
Here $RA=HM$ by the definitions of $A,H$; the source remains $(HM\otimes N)\otimes T$.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category) and 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent-written calculation from the displayed hypotheses; calculation Step 4

proof.text:
The assumed action identity for $(J,Q,\delta)$, evaluated at $(M,X,Y)$, is
$$\delta_{M_1,Y}(\delta_{M,X}\otimes1_Y)=J(c)\delta_{M,X\otimes Y}\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{A,X,Y}.$$
Compose on the right with $b_A$ of Step 2. The adjacent associator and its inverse cancel, giving the completely typed equality of maps $A\otimes V\to J(M_1\otimes QY)$:
$$\delta_{M_1,Y}(\delta_{M,X}\otimes1_Y)b_A=J(c)\delta_{M,X\otimes Y}(1_A\otimes u).$$
This uses just the two-sided inverse law for the associator in [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category) and 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent-written calculation from the displayed hypotheses; calculation Step 5

proof.text:
Naturality of $\delta$ in its second variable, applied to the arrow $u:V\to X\otimes Y$ in $\mathcal D$, gives
$$\delta_{M,X\otimes Y}(1_A\otimes u)=J(1_M\otimes Q(u))\delta_{M,V}.$$
Substitution into Step 5 and the composition law of $J$ give
$$\delta_{M_1,Y}(\delta_{M,X}\otimes1_Y)b_A=J\bigl(c(1_M\otimes Q(u))\bigr)\delta_{M,V}=J(b_M)\delta_{M,V}.$$
Thus the comparison with $P(N\otimes T)$ is accounted for by naturality along the specified $u$, rather than by an unmentioned coherence or an inverse of an action map.

source.place: Tags 0FFK (definition-monoidal-category) and 0FFL (definition-functor-monoidal-categories); agent-written calculation from the displayed hypotheses; calculation Step 6

proof.text:
Insert Step 6 into Step 4. Functoriality and the definitions of $H,\tau$ yield
$$\begin{aligned}
W&=H(b_M)R(\delta_{M,V})\pi_{A,N\otimes T}\alpha^{\mathcal E}_{HM,N,T}\\
&=H\bigl((\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{M,SN,ST})^{-1}(1_M\otimes\mu^S_{N,T})\bigr)\tau_{M,N\otimes T}\alpha^{\mathcal E}_{HM,N,T}.
\end{aligned}$$
Together with the definition of $W$, this is the required tensor-action identity. Naturality was proved in Step 1 and the explicit factorization in Step 3. Each substitution used only a given naturality or action equation, a functor law, or a specified associator inverse; no adjunction, symmetry or unit law for $\pi,\delta$ was used.
